questions.q: What is a missing dependency during Update Set preview?
options: The Update Set references a customization that lives in a different, not-yet-promoted Update Set
The target instance has no Update Sets at all
The Update Set was never completed in the source instance
Two Update Sets both reference the same unrelated table
questions.explain: A missing dependency occurs when something referenced by the set you're previewing hasn't arrived yet because it's packaged in a different Update Set.

questions.q: What is the correct fix for a missing-dependency error during preview, rather than forcing the set through?
options: Delete the Update Set and start over from scratch
Find and promote the earlier Update Set that contains the missing piece first, then re-run preview
Ignore the error since preview errors are always false positives
Manually recreate the missing component directly on the target instance
questions.explain: Promoting dependencies in the correct order resolves the real cause; forcing the set through does not make the missing component exist.

questions.q: Why do skipped records deserve deliberate review instead of being clicked past?
options: Skipped records are always errors that block the commit automatically
Skipping something that actually mattered can leave the target instance in a subtly broken state that won't surface until later
Skipped records have no effect on the target instance either way
ServiceNow automatically re-applies every skipped record during commit
questions.explain: A skipped record wasn't flagged as an error, but that doesn't mean it was safe to omit — it needs the same deliberate review as a collision.

questions.q: What real-world situation typically causes a partial commit?
options: A developer intentionally splits a commit into stages
The commit sequence is interrupted partway through, for example by a network drop, leaving some changes applied and others not
The Update Set contains no changes at all
The target instance rejects every record in the Update Set
questions.explain: An interruption mid-sequence, such as a network issue, can leave the target instance with some changes applied and others missing — a messy state needing careful investigation.

questions.q: Why do missing dependencies, skipped records, and partial commits compound when promoting several Update Sets together rather than one?
options: Because ServiceNow limits how many Update Sets can be promoted in a single day
Because a problem in one set can hide among the others being reviewed, and any one of several commits could be the one an interruption affects
Because multiple Update Sets cannot be previewed in the same session
Because these problems only ever occur with a single, isolated Update Set
questions.explain: A single, isolated Update Set rarely triggers all three problems; a multi-set release makes any one of them easy to miss amid everything else being promoted.
